newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP SAYS TO LOOK WITHIN FOR REPLACEMENTS.
newsitem.headline: BHP SAYS TO LOOK WITHIN FOR REPLACEMENTS.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd managing director JOhn Prescott said on Friday the board would look first within BHP for replacements for the three senior executives who resigned this week.

"The first steps will be a series of assessments within the organisation," Prescott told a media briefing called in the wake of the resignation on Friday of BHP Petroleum executive general manager John O'Connor.

O'Connor was the third senior executive to leave the company in three days following the departure of the head of the group's mineral division, Dick Carter, on Wednesday and the head of its iron ore unit, Geoff Wedlock, on Thursday.
Prescott said BHP had considerable talent within its ranks, particularly in the minerals division but it was not a case of simply appointing the most obvious candidate.

As a global organisation, he said BHP had to consider the career paths of its executives and the need to gain overseas experience. BHP had several suitable internal candidates for the positions held by both Carter and Wedlock, Prescott said.

"What we have to consider is what is the best mix of moving people around, not only to fill these positions ... but more importantly to establish a pattern of development going forward for the company and the individuals," he said.
